examples.en: You could at least have let me know.
Come for a short while at least.
She didn't even look at me.

related.en: at least — the minimum that could be expected
at least, even if — a concession, a minimal condition
even — emphasis, an unexpected degree

note: Ба̑р often sounds like a reproach: «you could at least have said so».

meanings: иако, упркос or без обзира на?

examples.sr: Све је прошло одлично, [и̏ако] смо очекивали најгоре.
examples.en: Everything went great, although we expected the worst.
He recovered quickly in spite of the doctor's prognosis.

examples.sr: Воз је стигао на време [без о̏бзира на] кашњење.
examples.en: The train arrived on time despite the delay.

related.en: although — before a whole clause
in spite of, against
regardless of, despite

note: И̏ако introduces a clause. У̏пркос takes the dative: упркос прогнози. Без о̏бзира на takes the accusative: без обзира на кашњење.

meanings: више or виши? боље or бољи?

examples.en: I like tea more than coffee.
He is taller than his brother.
I feel better today.
He is a better student than I am.
Dragan is the tallest in the class.
He is the one I love most.

related.en: more — adverb from «много»; највише - most
taller, higher — adjective from «висок»; највиши - tallest
better — adverb from «добро»; најбоље - best
better — adjective from «добар»; најбољи - the best

note: Ви̏ше̄ and бо̏ље̄ are adverbs, ви̏шӣ and бо̏љӣ are adjectives. Do not mix up ви̏ше̄ (more) and ви̏шӣ (taller).

examples.en: The child picked a flower.
I have to tidy up the room.

related.en: to pick, to gather — flowers, fruit; убрати шљиве
to tidy up, to put in order; to prepare — спремити собу, спремити ручак

note: У̀брати is to pick or gather a crop, not to tidy up: for that use спре́мити.

examples.en: I bought a pair of shoes.
Steam is coming out of the pot.
I don't have the money for that.
Smoke is coming out of the chimney.

related.en: pair; a couple, a few — брачни пар, пар дана
steam (water vapor)
money (colloq., pl.)
smoke

note: The plural па̏ре «money» has the genitive пара: немам пара - «I have no money».

examples.sr: Марко ми је [предло̀жио] да идемо на планину.
examples.en: Marko suggested that we go to the mountains.
They offered me a good job.
She treated us to cakes.

related.en: to suggest, to propose — an idea, advice, a candidate
to offer something concrete — a job, help, a price, marriage
to offer someone food or drink — понудити госта колачем

note: To offer coffee or a treat is по̀нудити, not предло̀жити, and the thing offered is in the instrumental: по̀нудити не̏кога не̏чим.

examples.en: Draw a straight line.
He is a true friend.
He is studying law in Belgrade.
Go straight to the traffic light.

related.en: straight (adj.) — права линија, права леђа
real, genuine — прави пријатељ
law; right (noun) — студирати право, имати право
straight ahead (adv.) — иди право

note: One form, many meanings: the context decides. Trap: пра̑вӣ means «real», not «correct»: a correct answer is та̏чан о̏дгово̄р.

examples.sr: Он је [љу̏бомо̄ран] јер му жена прича са колегом.
examples.en: He is jealous because his wife is chatting with a colleague.
He looks at her with envy.

related.en: jealousy — of a person, in love; љубоморан је на брата
envy — of someone else's things, success; завидети некоме

note: Strictly, љубо̀мора is jealousy and за́вист is envy, but in speech љу̏бомо̄ран is often said of envy too.

examples.en: This milk is good until tomorrow.
It's no use, you can't get through.
We'll have coffee on Saturday, okay?

related.en: to be good, fit for use; ought to — ово млеко ваља до сутра
to be worth; to be of use — овај прстен вреди 200 евра
to be valid, in force; okay, deal — пасош важи до...

note: Ваља also means «should»: ваљало би, ваља се. Не ваља is «no good»: не ваља ти то. Не вреди is «no use, pointless».

examples.en: The customer is satisfied.
There are a lot of swimmers at the beach.
I bought a new swimsuit.

related.en: buyer, customer — pl. купци
swimmer, bather — pl. купачи
swimming (adj.), swimsuit — купаћи костим

note: If the diacritics are dropped in Latin spelling, ку́пац and ку̀па̄ч look the same, and so do купачи and ку̀па̄ћӣ. Context tells them apart.

key: cmp:досадан-досадило ми је-досадно ми је-криво ми је-штета
meanings: досадно, досадило, штета or криво ми је?

examples.en: I'm bored in class.
I'm tired of waiting.
This movie is boring.
It's a pity you can't come.

examples.sr: [Кри̑во] ми је што ниси могла да дођеш.
examples.en: I'm sorry you couldn't come.

related.en: I'm bored
I'm sick of it, I've had enough
boring; annoying — досадан филм, не буди досадан
a pity, too bad
I'm sorry, I feel bad about it

meanings: comfortable or convenient: удобан, одговара or згодно?

examples.en: This chair is very comfortable.

examples.sr: Да ли ти [одго̀вара] да се видимо у девет?
examples.en: Does it suit you to meet at nine?

examples.sr: Да ли ти је [зго̏дно] да се видимо сутра?
examples.en: Is it convenient for you to meet tomorrow?

related.en: comfortable — of an object, physically
it suits me, it's convenient for me — of time, conditions
it's convenient, it suits — of time, place

note: У̀добан is only about physical comfort. «Awkward, uncomfortable» in the social sense is не̏прија̄тно: осећам се непријатно.

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је] што смо се упознали.
examples.en: I'm very glad we met.
Thank you, and the same to you (enjoy your meal).

related.en: nice to meet you, glad — when being introduced
enjoy your meal; all the best — at the table, when parting

note: При̏ја̄тно is not said when meeting someone: «nice to meet you» is дра̑го ми је.

examples.en: What kind of clothes do you wear?
What is your favorite color?
Whose decision is it?

related.en: what kind of — by quality, properties
which, what — from a known set
whose

note: All three decline like adjectives: by gender, number and case.

examples.en: What size are you?
Do you have size 39?

examples.sr: Ручни пртљаг не сме да прелази дозвољене [димѐнзије].
examples.en: Carry-on luggage must not exceed the permitted dimensions.

related.en: size in general — of clothes, things
size as a number; shoe size — број ципела
dimensions, measurements of an object

note: Димензије means only the dimensions of an object, not a clothing size.

meanings: зато што, јер, због тога што or зато?

examples.sr: Нисам те звао, [за̀то̄ што̏] је било касно.
examples.en: I didn't call you because it was late.
I didn't come because I was sick.

examples.sr: Закаснили смо [збо̏г то́га што̏] је била гужва.
examples.en: We were late because there was a traffic jam.
He was sick, so he didn't come.
We were late because of the traffic jam.

related.en: because
because, since — shorter, more common in speech
because of the fact that
so, that's why
because of — with the genitive

note: За̀то̄ means «so, that's why», not a conjunction of cause. Збо̏г is a preposition, због тога што a conjunction. More formal: по̏што, у̏след.

examples.en: The series is over.
Are you ready to go?
Lunch is ready, sit down.

related.en: done, finished — the process is complete, the result is in front of us
ready to start — everything is prepared for the action

note: Го̀тово also means «almost»: го̀тово бѐсплатно. Of lunch, both го̀тов and спре̏ман are used.

examples.en: The boss is on a business trip.
I'll take a week of vacation.
We're going on a summer vacation to Montenegro.
We're going on a winter vacation to Kopaonik.
The trip to Zagreb takes four hours.

related.en: trip, journey — пут у иностранство
vacation, time off; rest — узети одмор, бити на одмору
summer vacation — usually at the seaside
winter vacation — usually in the mountains, skiing

note: A business trip is a separate set phrase: слу̏жбенӣ пу̑т.

meanings: parts of the day: ујутру, преподне, подне, поподне, послеподне

examples.en: I drink coffee on the balcony in the morning.
The doctor sees patients only in the late morning.
We have lunch at exactly noon.
See you in the afternoon.
The kids come home from school in the late afternoon.
We were at the theater last night.

related.en: in the morning, roughly 3-9 a.m. — јуче ујутру
in the late morning, 9 a.m.-12 — no longer early morning
at noon, exactly 12
in the afternoon, 12-3 p.m. — right after noon
in the late afternoon, 3-6 p.m. — closer to evening
last night, yesterday evening / this evening / tonight

note: The hour boundaries are approximate. Trap: су̏тра means «tomorrow», not «in the morning»: «in the morning» is у̏јутру.

examples.sr: Како се зове она [ства̑р] за брисање пода?
examples.en: What's that thing for mopping the floor called?
This appliance makes shakes.

related.en: thing, item — any object; colloquially also «a song»
device, appliance — electrical or technical

note: A mop or a coffee pot is not an у̏ређа̄ј: it is a ства̑р.

examples.en: Our driver is waiting in front of the hotel.
The guide showed us the fortress.
The TV host announced the guest.
I passed my driving test on the first try.

related.en: host, presenter — on TV, radio
driver — of a bus, taxi
guide, tour guide
driver's license — short for возачка дозвола

note: The driver of a vehicle is во̀за̄ч, while во̀дитељ is the host of a program.

examples.en: I love you.
They kiss as they say goodbye.
I like you.

related.en: to love — a person, a thing, food
to kiss — љубити се means «to kiss each other»
to like, to be pleasing

note: Trap: «to love» is во̀лети, not љу́бити, which means «to kiss». With сви́ђати се, the person who likes is in the dative: свиђа ми се.

examples.en: The kids bop to the music.
We danced the kolo until morning.
They are dancing a waltz.

related.en: to dance — colloquial; on the spot, in time with fast music, of children
to dance — freely; a circle dance; fast couple dances
to dance — with choreography; slow couple dances

note: All three mean «to dance». Ѝграти and пле́сати are often interchangeable: Serbs themselves hardly distinguish the nuances.

meanings: days off: викенд, слободан дан, празник or нерадни дан?

examples.en: We're going to the seaside for the weekend.

examples.sr: Не радим уторком, тада имам [сло̏бодан да̑н].
examples.en: I don't work on Tuesdays, that's my day off.

examples.sr: У уторак не радимо јер је државни [пра̑знӣк].
examples.en: We don't work on Tuesday because it's a public holiday.

examples.sr: Петак нам је [не̏радни да̑н] због празника.
examples.en: Friday is a non-working day for us because of the holiday.

related.en: weekend, Saturday and Sunday — за викенд, продужени викенд
a personal day off — even if it falls on a Wednesday
public holiday — државни празник
non-working day — official, usually because of a holiday

note: Вѝкенд is only Saturday and Sunday; the other words depend on the reason for the day off.

examples.en: At school the kids eat a snack.
I made a delicious dinner.

related.en: snack, afternoon snack — at school, between meals
dinner, supper

note: У̏жина is a snack, not dinner: dinner is вѐчера.

examples.en: Draw it in pencil, then erase it.
Sign it with a ballpoint pen.

related.en: pencil — in conversation adults also use it for a pen
ballpoint pen — short form хемијска

note: Strictly, о̀ло̄вка is a pencil, but someone who asks for an о̀ло̄вка often means a pen. If you need a pen, ask for a хемијска.

examples.en: I drink red wine with meat.
White wine is better with fish.
Give us a bottle of red wine.

related.en: red wine — the more usual name, literally «black wine»
white wine
red wine — also understood, but less common

note: Serbs often call red wine literally «black»: црно вино.

examples.en: The flight to Belgrade takes two hours.
This summer we're going to the seaside.

related.en: flight — лет за Београд
summer — the season

note: The genitive of both words is лета; only the context tells them apart.

examples.en: We swam in the warm sea.
At night an awful nightmare tormented her.

related.en: sea — n., pl. мора
nightmare — f.

note: The plural of мо̏ра is spelled like мо̑ре: моје море can mean «my nightmares».

examples.en: Our teacher is very patient.
The math teacher is strict.

related.en: teacher — primary school, grades 1-4
subject teacher — from grade 5

note: Feminine forms: учитѐљица, на́ста̄вница.

examples.en: The city assembly approved the budget.

examples.sr: У [о̏пштини] се издају изводи из матичне књиге.
examples.en: Birth and marriage certificates are issued at the municipality office.
The local community council is organizing a meeting of residents.

related.en: assembly; parliament; city council
municipality — also where marriages and births are registered
local community council — self-government of the residents of a neighborhood

note: Without any qualification, ску̏пштина usually means the national parliament, while скупштина града is the city assembly.

examples.en: My car is in the garage.
Your cola is cold.
They danced the kolo until midnight.
The second round is the hardest.

related.en: car; the drink cola — n. pl. or f. sg.
kolo, a circle folk dance; round — n.

note: Agreement shows the meaning: ко̏ла су но̑ва - the car (pl.), кола је хладна - the drink (sg.).

key: cmp:пудер у камену-пудер у праху-течни пудер

examples.en: I apply loose powder with a big brush.

examples.sr: Увек носим [пу́дер у ка̀мену] у торбици.
examples.en: I always carry pressed powder in my purse.
I need liquid foundation for my face.

related.en: loose powder
pressed powder — compacted, solid
liquid foundation — in everyday speech often just «пудер»

note: In conversation, plain пу́дер often means foundation, not powder. To be exact, add у праху or у камену.

examples.en: Hit the brakes!
You're so clumsy!

related.en: brake — of a car or bicycle
clumsy, dopey — of an absent-minded, awkward person

note: Slowness is also described as као успорени снимак - «like slow motion».

examples.sr: Какав ти је то [фа̏зон]? Обећаш па не дођеш.
examples.en: What kind of behavior is that? You promise and then you don't show up.
What's the catch?

related.en: cut, style (of clothes); manner, way of doing things; a gag, a joke
a head start (in a game); a trick; a joke, a gag

note: They overlap only in the sense of «a joke»: «Ба̏ш је фо̏ра!» - «That's a good one!». «У свом фазону» - «true to form, in his usual style».

examples.en: He is a good man.
She is a very kind person.

related.en: man, person; more often, a man
person, individual — of either sex

note: Чо̏век often means «man». For a woman, or to be neutral, о̏соба is more usual: она је оптимистична особа.

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
Every morning I dress the kids for kindergarten.
Put your shoes on.
I don't like putting on new shoes.

related.en: to put on, to dress (pf.) — clothes
to put on, to dress (impf.) — clothes
to put on shoes (pf.)
to put on shoes (impf.)

note: Clothes take обући and облачити, shoes take обути and обувати. The imperatives о̏буци! and обуј! look alike but are not interchangeable.

meanings: чекати, сачекати, причекати, очекивати or дочекати?

examples.en: I waited for you for a long time in front of the school.
Wait for me until I finish.
Wait for me a little.
I didn't expect a gift.
They gave us a warm welcome.

related.en: to wait — the general word
to wait for, to wait until (pf.)
to wait a little
to expect, to count on something
to welcome guests; to live to see

note: Че̏кати, са̀чекати and прѝчекати are almost interchangeable. До̀чекати is either to receive guests or to finally live to see something: дочек Нове године - ringing in the New Year.

examples.en: Thank you for coming.
I think she is a good person.
I know what you're doing.

related.en: that, because — in set phrases: зато што, пре него што, све што
that — after opinions, feelings, knowledge: сматрам да, бојим се да
what — знам шта радиш

note: Rule of thumb: if you can insert «because», use што̏, if not, use да. As a question, што̏? means «why?» and шта̏? means «what?».

meanings: баш, јако, како or што in a compliment?

examples.en: You are very beautiful.
Wow, what a good-looking guy!
How beautiful you are!
How beautiful you are today!

related.en: very — simply intensifies the quality
really, indeed — conviction
how, what a — an exclamation
how, what a — an exclamation, close to «како»

note: Ка̏ко and што̏ open an exclamation: како си лепа!, што си лепа!. Ја̑ко and ба̏ш stand next to the adjective itself.

examples.en: Every morning I make breakfast for the kids.
For breakfast I cook porridge and eggs.

related.en: to prepare, to make — a universal word for any kind of food
to boil, to cook in a pot — only what is boiled

note: «To make breakfast» is usually спре́мати до̀ручак. For something that is boiled, ку̏вати fits: кувам чорбу.

examples.en: I have to submit a visa application.

examples.sr: Потписао је [и̏зјаву] да ништа није видео.
examples.en: He signed a statement that he had seen nothing.

related.en: application, request — filed to get something
statement — a person officially confirms something

note: An application is submitted: по̀дне̄ти за́хтев. A statement is given: дати изјаву.

meanings: рачун, признаница or уплатница: bill and receipt

examples.en: Give me the bill, please.
Keep the receipt in case you need it.

examples.sr: Попунила сам [у̀платницу] и платила у пошти.
examples.en: I filled out the payment slip and paid at the post office.

related.en: bill, check; cash register receipt — an amount to pay or a payment made
receipt, acknowledgment — money received
payment slip — for paying at a bank or post office

note: Ра̀чӯн is also a «bank account»: рачун у банци.

examples.en: Almost everyone has already left.
I got back from the seaside recently.
See you soon!
I'll come soon.

related.en: almost; recently
soon, shortly — about the near future

note: Trap: «soon» is у̏скоро, not ско̀ро, which means «almost» or «recently».

meanings: зашто, зато што or јер: why and because

examples.en: Why didn't you come?
I'm late because there is a traffic jam.
I didn't come because I was sick.

related.en: why — a question
because — an answer
because, since — a short conjunction

note: You ask with за̏што and answer with за̀то̄ што̏ or је̏р. Је̏р is shorter and more common in writing.

examples.en: Where are you going tonight?
Where is the library?

related.en: where (at) — place
where (to) — direction

note: In conversation где̏ is often used instead of ку̀да: где идеш?. The standard form is ку̀да.

examples.en: I see your shadow on the wall.
In summer we look for shade.

related.en: shadow, silhouette — the general word; сенка за очи - eye shadow
cool shade — where you can hide from the heat

note: Хладо̀вина comes from хла́дан, «cool». Deep shade is дебела хладовина.

examples.en: I study the Serbian language at the university.
I learn Serbian at home.

related.en: to study at a university; to study a subject as a student
to learn, to study — on one's own, in courses, at school

note: A schoolchild does not студира: he учи or goes у школу.

examples.en: He is a painter and does portraits.
She is an artist: she sings and acts.

related.en: painter — paints pictures
artist — music, theater, painting

note: Both can be translated as «artist», but сли̏ка̄р is only a painter, while у̀метнӣк is broader.

examples.en: He paints in oil on canvas.
I photographed the mountain from the top.
The child is drawing a house with a pencil.

related.en: to paint; in everyday speech, to take photos
to photograph — neutral, the standard word
to draw — in pencil, pen: lines, sketches, plans

note: From сли̏кати comes сли̏ка̄р, from цр̏тати comes цр́теж, a drawing. In everyday speech «take a picture of me» is сликај ме.

examples.en: I wash my hands before eating.
I have been following this series for years.

related.en: to wash — hands, laundry
to follow, to keep track of; to accompany — пратити вести, пратити некога

note: They sound alike, but the present tense forms differ: перем and пратим.

examples.en: I feel better today.
I remember that summer.

related.en: to feel (well, bad, etc.) — how one feels
to remember, to recall

note: Both have «се», but the meaning differs. After се̏ћати се comes the genitive: сећам се тог дана.

examples.en: I ask him where he lives.
I drink tea without sugar.

related.en: to ask — пита ме нешто
to drink

note: The present tense forms differ: пи̑та̄м and пи̏је̄м.

examples.en: I like her idea.
The brothers often quarrel.

related.en: to like, to be pleasing — свиђа ми се овај град
to quarrel — они се стално свађају

note: The one who likes is in the dative: свиђа ми се. To quarrel «with someone» takes «с» and the instrumental: свађам се с братом.

examples.en: I'm sending you a message.
We're celebrating the birthday on Saturday.

related.en: to send — шаљем, шаљеш
to celebrate, to honor — славити рођендан

note: The present tense forms differ: ша̏ље̄м and славим. «To send off» is also по̀слати.

examples.en: I waited for half an hour.
The trip takes an hour and a half.

related.en: half — before a noun: пола јабуке
and a half — after a numeral

note: Пола goes before the noun, «и по» after the numeral: по́ла са̑та, са̑т и по, два̑ и по са̑та.

examples.en: I'm sorry I was late.
It's a pity you can't come.

related.en: I'm sorry — a personal feeling
a pity, too bad — an assessment of the situation; damage

note: Жа̏о ми је also works as an apology: жао ми је што касним. Ште̏та also means «damage»: материјална штета.

meanings: преко, кроз or за: «across, through, in»

examples.en: We're crossing the bridge.
We're going through the forest.
I'll be there in five minutes.

related.en: across, over — on top of, on the other side: bridge, river, street
through — inside: tunnel, forest, crowd
in (time from now); for

note: «In five minutes» is за пе̑т мину́та. Кроз пе̑т мину́та also occurs, but less often.

examples.en: Maybe I'll come tomorrow.
He can swim.
Shall we go for coffee? - Sure!

related.en: maybe, perhaps — probability, does not change
can; may; okay — a form of the verb моћи, or agreement

note: «Maybe» is мо̀жда; ability, permission and agreement are може.

examples.en: I drive a bus every day.
Mom drives the kids to school.
I take the bus every day.

related.en: to drive; to give a ride — to operate a vehicle or carry someone
to ride; to go for a ride — as a passenger or for fun

note: Without «се» you are at the wheel, with «се» you are just riding. The vehicle is in the instrumental with no preposition: аутобусом, возом, колима.
